title: Publication Note
html:
Publication note

© 2026 Northeast Forests LLC. All rights reserved. Compiled by Steven Bick, Alison Berry and Maura Ross. Revised September 23, 2026. This edition incorporates reviewer comments, the supplied hyperlink audit and targeted checks of official agency and statutory sources. It contains 167 incentive entries, including seven federal entries, with sections for all 50 states. This is a screening guide, not a tax opinion or a guarantee of an award. It covers federal programs and all 50 states, but it is not an exhaustive inventory of local incentives, exemptions, grants or financing. A listing does not establish that applications are open or that a particular business, expense or tax return qualifies. Rates and examples are conditional on the eligibility facts stated. Taxpayer type, project location, timing, tax liability, allocations and agreements can change the usable benefit. Before committing funds or filing a return, confirm the current rules with the administering agency and a qualified tax adviser.

What changed

Credit amounts now lead each entry. Timing codes and repetitive state introductions have been removed. State navigation is alphabetical, with federal first. Examples distinguish total awards from annual use. Unrelated and closed new-award programs are omitted from the main listings. A maintenance protocol appears at the end.

Verification limits

The September 23 targeted review resolves the previous source flags except for two specific questions about Colorado training-credit carryforward and the New Hampshire research-credit cap transition. These qualifications appear with the affected entries and in the follow-up section. This is not an independent legal review of every entry; other unconfirmed rules remain identified where applicable.

title: How to Use This Sourcebook
html:
How to use this sourcebook

Start with the activity, not the equipment budget Use the national table to find a state, then its program index to find the relevant activity. A business may qualify as a taxpayer while a specific equipment purchase does not. Research, hiring and training credits therefore identify the activity separately from the business sector.

Read the green box first

The green box gives the credit amount or formula. It does not mean guaranteed eligibility or an immediate cash payment. The example then shows either a conditional calculation or a clearly labeled use-of-credit illustration when no reliable project award can be calculated.

Timing is written beside every credit

The amber box states the action or deadline in words. These are cumulative checkpoints, not mutually exclusive categories: a program can require advance approval and a later annual filing. An underway project is not automatically ineligible, and a tax-year credit is not automatically free of certification requirements.

Difficulty

Meaning

1 of 3 - Routine

Primarily employee, expense or tax-return

documentation; no negotiated project award.

2 of 3 - Certified

Separate application, certification, location test or substantial supporting records.

3 of 3 - Complex

Negotiation, competitive allocation, major technical review or continuing project compliance. Difficulty rates administrative effort, not the dollars invested. A high minimum investment is an eligibility condition, not by itself proof of application difficulty. Ratings are editorial screening judgments, not agency classifications.

Interpreting fit and value

Forest-products fit

Meaning

1 of 3 - Specialized

A narrow property, technology, ownership or

very-large-project route; ordinary mills should

not presume eligibility.

2 of 3 - Conditional

Potential fit depends on specific research,

geography, wages, investment, feedstock or

other project facts.

3 of 3 - Broad route

A comparatively broad route for eligible

forest-products businesses within the program's

business class; all program conditions still apply. A broad fit does not mean the credit is exclusive to forestry, that every logger qualifies, or that all property is eligible. Apply the most restrictive material condition when assessing a project. Compare actual dollars, not a subjective value score The former modest/meaningful/major rating is replaced by the formula and the example. A $25,000 benefit may be important to one business and minor to another. Compare the usable amount, timing, compliance cost and risk for your own business.

Distinguish four different amounts

Qualified spending is the accepted cost base. Credit earned is the result of the formula or award. Credit usable this year is the amount allowed against the relevant tax after caps. Cash received is limited to an authorized refund or transfer proceeds; a nonrefundable credit is not a grant.

Read the use rules

A carryforward preserves eligible unused credit for later years; it does not guarantee sufficient future tax. Transferability is a legal permission, not a guaranteed buyer or sale price. Credits can also be reduced or recaptured if commitments are not maintained. Do not assume state and federal incentives can be stacked on identical expenses.

title: Maintenance and Follow-Up
html:
Maintenance and source checks

A publication date is not a continuing guarantee. Use the following editorial process for the PDF and any website derived from it. This protocol does not itself create a monitoring service.

When

Editorial action

Monthly

Test links and redirects for relevant content. Record failures by program identifier and source title.

Quarterly

Review official notices, legislation, application windows, allocations and expiration dates. Prioritize unresolved entries.

Before tax

season

Check formulas and tax-use rules against the new forms and instructions, including carryforward, refunds, transfers and stacking.

Before

publication

Have a second reviewer check sources, recalculate examples and test links, contents, bookmarks and page numbers.

Maintain one structured record per incentive

Record the identifier, jurisdiction, agency, source, statute or form, eligibility, calculation, limits, tax-use rules, timing, example assumptions, verification date, reviewer and next review date. Archive superseded versions outside the reader-facing guide. Treat access restrictions separately from broken links An agency may block automated requests while its public page works in a browser. Record the access limitation without inferring repeal. A directory alone does not establish program rules; retain the relevant statute or form.

Keep the website and PDF synchronized

Generate both from the same reviewed records, with record-review and publication dates. After substantive changes, recalculate examples and regenerate navigation. Updating the year alone is insufficient.

Items requiring a follow-up

check

These items are not represented as fully resolved. They should be checked before relying on the affected program. Unconfirmed carryforward periods are also stated within individual entries.

Entry

Remaining check

Job Training Credit

The 2026 amendment places a 14-year

carryforward paragraph within the

training subsection but refers to

investment-credit subsection (1). Confirm

the Department of Revenue interpretation

and covered credit years before relying on

any training-credit carryforward period.

New Hampshire - Research

and Development Tax

Confirm whether the $50,000 or $100,000

taxpayer cap applies to calendar-year

2026 research submitted by June 30,

2027. The higher cap takes effect January

1, 2027, but the applicable agency

application-cycle instructions were not

available in the targeted review.

Project-specific determinations

Resolve taxpayer eligibility, the actual wood feedstock and equipment definitions, new-award availability, remaining annual allocation and binding-commitment dates directly with the agency. Directory links and screening ratings cannot substitute for a written project determination.

Review date

Revised September 23, 2026, using the September 22 hyperlink audit and the September 23 targeted verification findings. The two questions above replace the previous nine-entry source-check list. Other entry-specific uncertainties remain as stated. Future legislation, agency notices and tax-year forms can supersede this edition.

title: Publication Staff
html:
Publication Staff

Steven Bick, PhD, CF

Steven Bick, PhD, CF, is a forest economist, consultant, and author who leads Northeast Forests LLC and directs The Forest Business School. His work spans the Northeast, Lake States, and Intermountain West, helping forest enterprises, landowners, and rural communities turn complex economic questions into practical business decisions. His experience includes business planning, financial analysis, pricing, operations, succession, and technology adoption. Through consulting, teaching, publications, and digital tools, he translates applied forest economics into strategies that help businesses evaluate opportunities, improve performance, and prepare projects for financing and implementation.

Alison Berry

Alison Berry is the owner of Woodland Resources LLC, a research consulting firm based in Bozeman, Montana. She brings more than 20 years of research experience spanning natural sciences, economics, policy, and land use, with expertise in forest products market analysis, biomass utilization, and technical writing. Her strengths include managing and interpreting data, explaining technical concepts to general audiences, and collaborating with diverse partners. Her work helps businesses and natural resource professionals understand market conditions, assess wood utilization opportunities, and apply research to practical decisions.

Maura Ross

Maura Ross brings expertise in wood innovation, wood energy, funding pathways, and applied project development. Her work supports forest products businesses in evaluating new uses for wood fiber and identifying resources to advance promising projects. She combines knowledge of wood utilization opportunities with an understanding of funding and implementation needs to help businesses move from initial concepts toward practical next steps.

title: Custom Guides and Additional Information
html:
Custom guides and additional

information

Guides and searchable websites for your audience We compile state-specific guides and develop searchable websites on tax incentives and other topics. These resources can be tailored to the needs of businesses, associations, public agencies, and regional organizations, bringing relevant information, practical examples, and source links together in a format readers can use. Contact us through the websites below to discuss a publication or online resource for your audience.

Corrections and new information

We intend to update this guide annually. We welcome corrections, updated links, and information about new or changed incentives. Please include the program name, state, relevant page or record identifier, and an official source when available. Reach us through Northeast Forests or Woodland Resources using the websites below so we can evaluate the information for the next edition.

Additional information

Visit these websites for additional information about our work and resources

for forest enterprises:

www.northeastforests.com

www.loggingchance.com

www.forestenterprise.org
